summary: Session 1 of 3: fleshed out the stub spec with locked design decisions (modal MudDialog from the Users-and-Role-Assignment tab; new BackofficeUserCreationService in Dabbler.Security with email-uniqueness via the existing AppUser.Email unique index + DbUpdateException catch; reject duplicate emails; IsProvisioned flag on AppUser defaulting to true with the admin INSERT explicitly opting in to false; new SensitiveAccessEventKind.UserCreated audit emitted INSIDE the EF transaction before the IsProvisioned flip; library scope split — dialog in Dabbler.Security.Blazor, service in Dabbler.Security, controller in AcmeCoffeeOnline.Api). Per-session step lists, API contract, audit plan, and risk notes (including post-commit magic-link enqueue failure mitigation) committed. Cross-provider verification round 1 found 1 Critical + 2 Major + 3 Minor design issues; all addressed; round 2 returned VERIFIED. No code changes in this session — Session 2 implements the API + service + unit tests; Session 3 implements the Razor dialog + UAT checklist + W2.

reason.specifics: Session 1 was design-heavy (opus-class) and warranted Opus 4.7. Session 2 is systematic C# implementation against a fully-fleshed-out spec: schema migration, BackofficeUserCreationService with one EF transaction, controller endpoint, unit tests covering happy path + UserAdmin cross-org rejection + CrossOrgMonitor denial + duplicate-email handling + transaction rollback on authority denial. Sonnet 4.6 at high effort is well-matched to this work mix and avoids burning Opus rates on mechanical-but-careful implementation.
